artifact_class_note: Each control states whether it hands off the current share-safe URL, a safer canonical public pointer, or a bounded text/contact artifact instead of leaving the artifact class implicit.
authority_context_minimum_note: Copied/shared artifacts preserve enough office, route, freshness, and recovery context to remain checkable later without turning every handoff into a full printable record.
clipboard_or_share_permission_note: Clipboard and native-share controls are reviewed for secure-context, activation, and policy boundaries without making capability success the price of reaching the official answer/help lane.
copy_share_surface_label: Example State official voter-information copy/share control posture
copy_success_truthfulness_note: The route does not announce copy success until clipboard write completes or a truthful fallback confirms the copied artifact is available.
delivery_role_note: Official copy/share controls hand off bounded public pointers or snippets without overstating what left the page, whether the handoff actually succeeded, or whether the current route was safe to forward directly.
native_share_boundary_note: Native share targets are treated as convenience handoffs only; final formatting and target availability are outside office control.
share_safe_substitution_note: If the current live route is not safely forwardable, the control substitutes a safer canonical official pointer or bounded public summary instead of copying the unsafe stateful URL.
share_success_truthfulness_note: The route keeps completed handoff, user cancel, unsupported environment, blocked policy, and transmission failure visibly distinct enough that opening a share sheet is not mislabeled as successful sharing.
unsupported_or_denied_fallback_note: When native share or clipboard support is unavailable or blocked, the route preserves a visible fallback such as a share-safe URL, durable record, or authoritative help path.
